A long glass tube (liquid-in-glass thermometer) lying horizontally. At the left end is a silver bulb (mercury). A thin red or silver line (capillary tube) runs down the center of the stem, ending at the 12 cm mark. The stem is marked with a scale starting from 0 cm (aligned with a "0 °C" label below it for the ice point) and ending at 20 cm, with a "100 °C" label below the 20 cm mark.

Three vertical thermometer scales placed side-by-side. The left one is, the middle is "Kelvin (K)", and the right is "Fahrenheit (°F)". Three horizontal dashed lines cut across all three scales: the top line is and intersects at 100 °C, 373 K, and 212 °F. The middle line is and intersects at 0 °C, 273 K, and 32 °F. The bottom line is and intersects at -273 °C, 0 K, and -459.67 °F.

A line graph showing the calibration of a thermometer. The vertical axis is "Temperature (°C)" from 0 to 100. The horizontal axis is "Thermometric Property, X". A straight diagonal line starts at the point (X₀, 0) and goes up to the point (X₁₀₀, 100). Dashed lines show how an unknown property X_θ on the horizontal axis maps to an unknown temperature θ on the vertical axis.
